Looking for personalized gum therapy in Austin, TX? At Enamel Dentistry, we help you prevent, halt, and treat gum disease with diode laser deep cleanings, scaling and root planing, and a calm, prevention-first team. Early gum disease rarely hurts, which is exactly why professional screening matters. Schedule Your Visit Call Us Diode laser deep cleanings · 9 Austin studios from South Lamar to Leander, plus McKinney 1–3 mm Healthy pocket depth 3–4 mo Maintenance cadence, higher risk 100+ Insurance plans accepted 10 Studios across Austin & McKinney Why it matters Gum disease is serious. Inflammation and bacteria can enter your bloodstream and contribute to heart disease, strokes, and harder-to-manage diabetes. Most of it is silent until it is not. Early gum disease rarely causes pain, which makes professional screening vital for preventive care. Stage 1 gingivitis is completely reversible. Later stages are not. At Enamel, we view gum disease as a spectrum — beginning with subtle bleeding and early gum recession, and, when left untreated, progressing through attachment loss to tooth loss. The earlier we catch you on it, the lighter the fix. Patients with gum disease have a 2–3 times higher risk of heart attack or stroke. Treating the gums lowers C-reactive protein, the inflammation marker your cardiologist already cares about. What happens at a periodontal visit From probe to plan, in plain English. Calm, methodical, and built around your numbers. No alarmist commentary while you are in the chair. 01 Probe, chart, X-ray We measure every pocket around every tooth with a periodontal probe, chart anything past 3mm, and pull digital X-rays to see what is happening at the bone. We also include an oral cancer screening at the same visit. ~10 min 02 Plain-English diagnosis Healthy gums, gingivitis, or active periodontitis. We tell you exactly what your numbers mean, where the trouble spots are, and what is reversible at this stage. ~5 min 03 Targeted deep cleaning Scaling and root planing below the gumline to clear hardened tartar and bacteria. Local anesthesia keeps the area completely numb. Diode laser, where indicated, speeds healing. ~30 min per quadrant 04 Maintenance plan A personalized schedule (often every 3 to 4 months) plus simple at-home guidance. We re-probe at every visit so progress is measured, not guessed. ~10 min The four stages of gum disease Know where you are. Treat what is still reversible. Most people land on this spectrum somewhere. The earlier we meet you on it, the simpler the fix. Here is what each stage looks like, and what we do about it. Anything past3 mmgets flaggedHealthy pockets read at three millimetres or less. We measure every tooth, every visit, so we can spot the half-millimetre that matters before it becomes the four that does not heal on its own. Stage 01Gingivitis1–3mmPocket depthRed, swollen gums that bleed easily at the flossing line. Caused by plaque buildup. Cleared with a professional cleaning and consistent home care.Fully reversible Stage 02Early periodontitis4–5mmPocket depthEarly attachment loss as gum tissue separates from the tooth, forming pockets. Treated with scaling and root planing, often paired with a diode laser to speed healing.Halt & manage Stage 03Moderate periodontitis6mmPocket depthDamage to the ligaments and surrounding bone, sometimes with early furcation involvement on multi-rooted teeth. Deep cleaning plus targeted antibiotic microspheres (Arestin), with closer maintenance.Manage progression Stage 04Advanced periodontitis7mm+Pocket depthSignificant bone loss and tooth mobility. For patients managing active periodontitis or diabetes, the ADA recommends periodontal maintenance every three to four months. TMJ disorder is what happens when the joints, muscles, and bite that move your jaw stop working together. Pain shows up in the jaw, the temples, the ears, the neck. The root cause is rarely the place it hurts. Stress, clenching, grinding, an old injury, or a bite that has shifted are the usual suspects. At Enamel Dentistry, our Austin dentists evaluate your airway, coordinate a sleep study or home sleep test with your physician, and fit a custom oral appliance (a mandibular advancement device) you can actually wear every night. For people who never got along with a CPAP machine, it’s often the first obstructive sleep apnea treatment that finally sticks. Schedule Your Visit Call Us Dentist-led, physician-coordinated · A real alternative to CPAP Evaluation · about 45 minutes★★★★★4,000+ five-star reviewsFrom real Austin patients ~45 minInitial airway evaluation2–4 wksTypical appliance turnaroundMedicalInsurance often covers10Austin & McKinney locations What it is Not snoring. A medical condition called obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The airway closes, breathing pauses (apneas and hypopneas), and the brain pulls you back out of deep sleep dozens, sometimes hundreds, of times a night. AHI severityMild · 5–14Mod · 15–29Severe · 30+ Sleep apnea is what happens when your airway collapses during sleep and your body keeps having to rescue it. The damage is not what happens overnight. It is what happens over years. Untreated, it raises the risk of heart disease, stroke, and diabetes. Most patients have lived with it for years before being diagnosed. Bed partners notice it first. By the time you walk in, you have usually been compensating with caffeine, naps, or just accepting the exhaustion as normal. We evaluate the airway, the jaw, and the bite together. Treatment is coordinated with your physician, who confirms the diagnosis with a sleep study. We design the oral appliance that fits how you actually sleep. Where it happensABAThe collapse. Tongue and soft tissue fall back, sealing the airway shut.BThe fix. A mandibular advancement device gently holds the lower jaw forward, holding the airway open. Symptoms & long-term impact Sleep apnea symptoms we hear most often. Sleep apnea symptoms rarely show up alone. Most patients describe a cluster: snoring plus morning headaches, or daytime exhaustion plus brain fog and high blood pressure that will not budge. If two or three of these sound familiar, it is time to be evaluated. ABCDWhy it mattersThe damage shows up far from the airway.ABrain. Fatigue, fog, mood changes, accident risk.BHeart. Higher risk of Type 2 diabetes. 01Loud, chronic snoringNightly snoring loud enough that a partner notices or sleeps in another room. Often the first clue. 02Waking up gaspingSudden gasping, choking, or a feeling of being briefly unable to breathe. The body is rescuing the airway. 03Morning headachesA dull, pressure-type headache already present at wake-up, from a night of low oxygen and disrupted sleep. 04Daytime sleepinessExhaustion that does not improve with a full night in bed. Falling asleep in meetings, while reading, or at the wheel. 05Brain fog & memory lapsesTrouble focusing, short-term memory slips, mood changes, irritability that landed without an obvious cause. 06Dry mouth or sore throatWaking with a sandpaper mouth or a raw throat, especially if you sleep on your back. 07Frequent night wakingSeveral trips to the bathroom or restless waking, often blamed on hydration but driven by airway disruption. 08Teeth grinding (bruxism)Worn enamel, flat edges, or jaw soreness on waking. A filling no one can see. Bonded to the tooth, matched to your shade, and finished in a single visit. Composite dental fillings are made from a durable resin material that bonds directly to your tooth. Unlike traditional metal fillings, they are designed to match the color of your natural teeth, creating a seamless and attractive result. These fillings are ideal for repairing small to medium cavities and for enhancing the appearance of worn or chipped teeth. Composite fillings not only restore function but also protect your tooth from further decay. White fillings are especially popular for front teeth because they are virtually invisible, giving patients confidence in their smiles. Shade-matchedComposite resin is color-matched to your tooth before it is placed, then polished to the same sheen as the enamel around it. Why composite Why should I choose composite fillings in Austin? Tooth-colored fillings do more than look good. They protect the tooth, restore the bite, and stop small problems from becoming big ones, all without the metal. Prevents More DecayBy removing decay and sealing the tooth with composite dental fillings, bacteria and food particles are blocked from entering, helping prevent cavity fillings from worsening. Early treatment protects your teeth and saves you from more extensive dental work later.Restores FunctionA tooth colored cavity filling restores your tooth’s integrity, allowing normal biting and chewing without pain or discomfort. Patients regain full function while keeping their natural smile intact.Aesthetically PleasingWhite fillings are designed to blend seamlessly with your natural teeth. Composite resin fillings can be color-matched precisely, giving you a natural-looking dental filling that enhances your smile.Stop Severe ProblemsUntreated cavities can worsen, eventually reaching the tooth’s nerve and causing abscesses or the need for a root canal. Cavity treatment with composite fillings prevents severe dental issues before they develop, protecting both your health and your smile. What to expect Your composite filling in a single, comfortable visit. Most fillings are placed start to finish in about an hour, with nothing to take home but a tooth that looks and works like new. 01Numb & prepareA small amount of local anesthetic keeps the tooth completely comfortable. We isolate the area so it stays clean and dry while we work.~10 min02Remove the decayWe gently clear away the decayed tissue, the dental caries that caused the cavity, and clean the area, removing only what needs to go and preserving as much healthy tooth as possible.~10 min03Bond & layerThe tooth is prepared with acid etching and a bonding agent, then color-matched composite resin is placed in thin layers, each cured firm with a curing light for a strong, sealed restoration.~15 min04Shape & polishWe sculpt the filling to fit your bite, check it feels natural, and polish it to the same sheen as the enamel around it. You leave the same day.~10 min Why Enamel Fillings that look like they were never there. A cavity should not cost you your smile. We treat composite fillings as cosmetic work, not just a repair. A dental crown is a custom-made cap that fits completely over a damaged tooth. It restores the tooth's strength, shape, and appearance. It also protects against further damage. Crowns are made from several materials Porcelain or ceramic: Natural-looking and ideal for front teeth Metal or metal alloys: Maximum strength, best for back molars Porcelain-fused-to-metal (PFM): Balances durability with a natural appearance Zirconia: Strong, tooth-colored, and biocompatible Our team uses precise digital scans to make every step of your crown treatment smooth and efficient. BridgesWhat is a dental bridge? A dental bridge replaces one to three consecutive missing teeth. It anchors onto surrounding teeth or implants (called abutments) and uses artificial teeth called pontics to fill the gap. This restores chewing and speaking function. It also prevents remaining teeth from drifting out of alignment. Bridges come in four main types Traditional bridges: Crowns on adjacent teeth support the pontic Maryland bridges: A pontic held by thin wings bonded to the backs of neighboring teeth, with little to no reshaping Implant-supported bridges: Anchored to dental implants for added stability Cantilever bridges: Attached on one side only, used in specific cases Why crowns & bridgesBenefits of dental crowns and bridges. Maybe you stopped noticing it. Maybe you catch it in every photo. Bonding closes it without braces and without filing your teeth down. We tint composite to match your enamel, build up the edges, and the gap is just gone. Most people are in and out in one sitting, a block from the Plaza Saltillo station. At Enamel Dentistry, good care starts with knowing your options. At our East Austin studio we walk your family through every choice before anyone sits in the chair. Chips, gaps, worn edges. Bonding sculpts them away by hand, in a single sitting. The basics What Is Dental Bonding, and How Does It Close a Gap? Bonding uses a tooth-colored resin called composite. We shade it to your enamel, brush a little bonding agent on the tooth, then add the resin and shape it by hand. A curing light sets it. To close a gap, a diastema if you want the real word, we widen the two front teeth toward each other by a hair on each side. Done right, you cannot see where your tooth ends and the composite starts.Here is the part people like. There is usually no drilling and no shot. We are adding to the tooth, not cutting into it. Nothing is wrong with the tooth’s health. You just want it to look different, and this is the gentlest way to get there. What that means for you Built right on the tooth. The resin is layered and shaped in the chair. There’s no impression sent to a lab and no temporary to wear while you wait.Conservative by design. We preserve your natural enamel wherever possible, which keeps the tooth strong and your options open down the road.Sculpted by hand. We rebuild an edge, close a gap, or refine a shape through gentle reshaping. That reshaping has a clinical name, enameloplasty, but it comes down to a trained eye rather than a mold.Matched to your shade. We select a resin color to disappear into your natural teeth, so the work is seen, not noticed. Why Enamel Why bonding here looks like bonding should Composite bonding is only as good as the material and the hand behind it. Two visits to two offices can produce two very different smiles. Here’s where we put our effort. What sets our work apart We invest in high-quality materials. Better composites hold their polish, resist wear, and blend more naturally than the bargain resin used to cut corners.Providers skilled in the art, not just the procedure. Several of our dentists are genuinely gifted at cosmetic sculpting and clinical photography, the difference between a fix and a result you’re proud of.Honest options, never over-treatment. If bonding is right, we’ll bond. If veneers or a crown would truly serve you better, we’ll tell you straight.Most cases, one visit. Multiple teeth can often be treated the same day, so you walk out with a noticeably improved smile. What it fixes The fixes East Austin folks come in for Most people come in about one thing they want to change, not a long list. Here is what bonding handles well. Closes the gap This is the one that brings most East Side folks in. A space between the front teeth, closed in a single visit, no metal and no aligners. A small gap or a wider one, we can do it. If it is really wide, we will tell you straight whether bonding alone gets there. Reshapes a tooth that is the wrong size If one tooth sits a touch small or short next to its neighbor, we build it out so the pair matches. Smooths a rough or chipped edge Caught a corner on a bottle out on Rainey? We can round the edge back so it feels right under your tongue again. Veneer look, less of the cost Bonding gets a lot of the same look as veneers for a lot less, and we do not grind the tooth to do it. Fair trade-off: it is not quite as tough, so we talk lifespan up front. Whiten first, then match Planning to whiten? Do that first. We match the composite to your brightened teeth the day we close the gap, so it blends in and stays blended. A fresh start, by the train New to the East Side and finally dealing with it? One visit, a block from Plaza Saltillo, and the thing you have meant to fix for years is done. How it works How composite bonding works: sculpted by hand, matched to your smile. Bonding is part craft, part chemistry. In direct composite bonding, the same materials used in modern tooth-colored fillings are shaped right on the surface of your tooth, then bonded and cured into place, no drilling away healthy structure, no metal, no dark margins.The strength of the result comes down to two things: the quality of the composite and the skill of the hand shaping it. We invest in both. An honest note: composite is beautiful and conservative, but it isn't quite as stain-resistant as porcelain. A few simple habits, plus a night guard, keep it looking its best for years. More on that below. Composite resin, layered Tooth-colored resin is applied and built up in thin layers right on the tooth. No lab, no impressions, no waiting. Hand-sculpted to shape Your provider works by hand here, rebuilding an edge, easing a gap shut, shaping each tooth to suit your face and your bite. Cured & polished A curing light sets the material in seconds. Then we polish it down to a smooth finish that catches light like a real tooth. Shade-matched to blend We choose a resin shade to disappear into your surrounding teeth, so the result is seen but never noticed. What to expect Your bonding appointment, step by step. Each tooth takes about 30 to 60 minutes, and most cases are finished in one visit. Here’s exactly how it goes. 01 Smile evaluation We review your teeth, talk through your goals, and select a resin shade to match your natural smile. 02 Tooth preparation We lightly etch the surface so it is a touch rough, which gives the bonding agent something to hold onto. Little to no enamel is removed. 03 Composite application The resin goes on in thin layers, shaped by hand as it builds up. 04 Curing & polishing A few seconds under the curing light and it is set. We then polish it smooth and natural. 05 Immediate results You’ll see the difference right away. Most cases are completed in a single visit. Sedation is hardly ever necessary for this. They picture going under and waking up groggy, the whole ordeal. Laughing gas isn’t that, not even close, and the folks who come to our Grove studio usually want to know why before they’ll believe it. Fair enough. It’s the mildest thing on the menu, breathed in through a little mask, and it’s out of your system minutes after we pull the mask off. Stick with this page and I’ll tell you how it actually works. Then you can make up your own mind. Schedule Your Visit Call (512) 884-5658 Breathe it through a nose mask · awake, calm, and you drive yourself home Relax through your whole visit ★★★★★4,000+ five-star reviewsFrom real Grove patients Nose mask Breathe it in, no pill or needle Awake Clear in minutes, drive yourself home 100+ Insurance plans accepted 10 Locations across Texas The basics A calm, awake way to get the dental care you’ve been putting off. Been away too long? Nitrous sedation makes coming back easy. The basicsWhat nitrous sedation isYou breathe nitrous oxide through a small mask over your nose, mixed with oxygen. Within a couple of minutes you feel warm and a little floaty, but you are fully awake and breathing on your own the whole time.You can still answer a question or lift a hand if you need something. Most people just lose track of the visit. The sounds and the poking that usually set your nerves off fade into the background.For anyone searching for laughing gas or nitrous sedation in The Grove, it is the lightest, most convenient option there is, and it clears in minutes so you can usually drive yourself home.Good candidatesWhen nitrous sedation makes senseIt is a good fit if dental anxiety has kept you away, if you have a stubborn gag reflex, or if you have a stretch of treatment to get through and would rather not feel every minute of it.Nitrous sedation often helps ifDental anxiety has kept you from coming in.A strong gag reflex makes cleanings hard to sit through.You have a backlog of work to catch up on.You would rather combine treatment into fewer visits.A past dental experience left you on edge. Serving Central Austin & the 38th St corridor The lightest option, explained. Being a stone’s throw from the 38th Street medical corridor, we get plenty of patients who read the label and ask the follow-up question. So I won’t be vague with you. What everybody calls laughing gas is nitrous oxide. You won’t see it or smell it, and we run it mixed with oxygen through a little mask over your nose. That’s the whole delivery system. The part that should give you confidence is how long it’s been around. Dentists have used this stuff since the 1800s, and not much in medicine survives that long without earning it.What it does is simple. Within a couple of minutes you feel warm and a little loose, sometimes a touch floaty. It quiets the nervous tension without switching off your awareness, so you’re talking with us the whole time and fully in control. The reason it’s considered the lightest option comes down to how fast it leaves. Once the mask is off and you breathe plain oxygen for a few minutes, the gas is out of your system. There’s no lingering grogginess, which is also why most people drive themselves home.That’s really the whole pitch, and it’s an honest one. Nitrous won’t put you under, and it isn’t the right tool for someone who needs deep sedation for a long, complex case. What it is good at is taking ordinary nervousness or a fussy gag reflex and making a normal visit easy, with basically no downside afterward. If you’ve been curious whether the mildest option is enough for you, it usually is, and we’re glad to talk it through. What to expect How a nitrous visit works, step by step There’s no prep and no needle for the gas itself. Here’s how a laughing-gas visit goes from the moment you sit down. 01Health review & planningWe go over your medical history, your medications, any allergies, and how anxious you tend to feel. That tells us whether laughing gas is the right fit. There is nothing to take ahead of time, and no needle for the gas itself.02The mask goes onA small, soft mask rests over your nose and you breathe a gentle mix of nitrous oxide and oxygen. When you arrive we get you settled and comfortable. No pill, and no injection for the sedation itself.03Settling into calmWithin two or three minutes the tension drains off and most people feel warm and a little floaty while staying fully awake. The visit feels shorter and easier than you remember dental visits being.04Care, closely watchedWe track your breathing, pulse, and oxygen the entire time. We numb as needed and move at an unhurried pace, telling you what is happening as we go.05Clear-headed, and you drive yourselfWhen we finish, you breathe plain oxygen for a few minutes and the gas clears out of your system. Most people feel completely normal within five to ten minutes, so in most cases you simply drive yourself home and get on with your day.06Aftercare & check-inMost people feel like themselves again by evening. We follow up afterward, and if you are coming back for more of your catch-up list, we fine-tune the plan based on how this visit went. Who it helps Who laughing gas is for.
